The catalyst comes pre-loaded in a sealed CatCart, so pyrophoric material never gets handled directly, and there's no filtration step afterward to separate it from your product. It runs from atmospheric pressure and room temperature up to 100 bar and 100°C, reaching those conditions in minutes, at a scale from milligrams to grams.

faqs.question: What is the H-Cube® Mini Plus used for?
faqs.answer: It's a continuous flow reactor used for catalytic hydrogenation and related reactions, generating hydrogen gas on demand without a cylinder, from milligram to gram scale.

faqs.question: How does on-demand hydrogen generation work?
faqs.answer: Hydrogen is generated by electrolysis of water inside the system itself, removing the need for a hydrogen gas cylinder in the lab.

faqs.question: How do I run a hydrogenation reaction on the H-Cube Mini Plus?
faqs.answer: Load a CatCart with your catalyst, let the system stabilize at your chosen pressure, temperature, and flow rate using solvent, then switch the input to your reactant solution; the product collects catalyst-free in the vial.

faqs.question: How do I choose between a pre-packed and a user-fillable CatCart?
faqs.answer: Use a pre-packed CatCart if a ready-made option exists for your target reaction, confirmed by Inkarp, or a user-fillable CatCart if you need to load a custom catalyst.

faqs.question: Can I perform deuteration reactions on this system?
faqs.answer: Yes. Deuteration is confirmed as a supported reaction, alongside standard hydrogenation chemistry.

faqs.question: What other reactions can I perform besides hydrogenation?
faqs.answer: Deuteration, Sonogashira coupling, and Suzuki coupling are confirmed supported reactions beyond standard hydrogen gas chemistry.

faqs.question: What water quality does the system require?
faqs.answer: Deionized water with a maximum conductivity of 71 nS/cm (minimum resistance 14 MΩcm).

faqs.question: What is the difference between the H-Cube Mini Plus and the H-Cube Pro?
faqs.answer: Full comparison detail is confirmed by Inkarp; contact our team for the specific differences relevant to your application.

faqs.question: Can the H-Cube Mini Plus be used by undergraduate students?
faqs.answer: This is confirmed by Inkarp based on your teaching lab's specific setup and supervision requirements.

faqs.question: What is the price of the H-Cube® Mini Plus in India?
faqs.answer: The price depends on the CatCart configuration and accessories your application needs. Contact Inkarp for a quotation once your target reactions are confirmed.

faqs.answer: Inkarp is the authorized distributor and service provider for the ThalesNano H-Cube® Mini Plus in India, providing demonstration, installation, training, AMC, spare parts, and technical support.

sections.title: How Continuous Flow Hydrogenation Works
body: The whole process runs as a continuous flow, not a batch reaction sitting in a flask.

Hydrogen is generated on demand by electrolysis of water, right inside the system. An HPLC pump brings in pure solvent, which mixes with that hydrogen through a mixing valve, and the resulting gas-liquid mixture runs through the reaction zone while the system stabilizes at your chosen pressure, temperature, and flow rate. Once those conditions are reached, you switch the input from solvent to your actual reactant solution. The reaction happens as the mixture passes through the packed CatCart column, where the solid catalyst stays behind while the product moves on to the collection vial.

A built-in mass flow controller doses in-situ hydrogen at 99.9% purity, or switches to any of 13 external gases, from oxygen and carbon monoxide to argon and ethylene, through the same external gas inlet. faqs.question: What is the H-Cube® Advance used for?
faqs.answer: It's a continuous flow reactor used for catalytic hydrogenation, catalyst screening, and related reactions, running on in-situ hydrogen or any of 13 external gas types.

faqs.question: What gases can the H-Cube Advance run besides hydrogen?
faqs.answer: Oxygen, nitrogen, carbon monoxide, carbon dioxide, air, argon, ethylene, ethane, methane, helium, nitrous oxide, nitrogen monoxide, and external hydrogen, all through the built-in mass flow controller.

faqs.question: How do I set up the H-Cube Advance for a reaction requiring an external gas?
faqs.answer: Confirm your required gas is on the supported list, connect it through the external gas inlet, and the built-in mass flow controller doses it precisely alongside your solvent and reactant stream.

faqs.question: How do I automate catalyst screening on the H-Cube Advance?
faqs.answer: Connect the Brooks AIM3300 Autosampler via the THS System Controller, which automates continuous liquid sample handling for unattended optimization studies or catalyst screening.

faqs.question: What is the difference between the H-Cube Advance and the H-Cube Mini Plus?
faqs.answer: The Advance supports 13 external gas types beyond hydrogen, reaches a wider temperature range (0 to 150°C versus ambient to 100°C), and connects to fleet modules the Mini Plus doesn't support; the Mini Plus is a more compact, standard-hydrogenation-only system.

faqs.question: What is the Phoenix Flow Reactor?
faqs.answer: An optional add-on module with an extended parameter window, up to 450°C and 200 bar, for synthesizing novel compounds beyond the base system's range.

faqs.question: Is the H-Cube Advance compatible with an autosampler?
faqs.answer: Yes, with the Brooks AIM3300 Autosampler, connected via the THS System Controller for fully automated liquid sample handling.

faqs.question: What is the purity of the hydrogen produced in-situ?
faqs.answer: 3.0 grade, 99.9% purity.

faqs.question: Does the H-Cube Advance need external equipment to run?
faqs.answer: Only an external ThalesNano HPLC or Knauer pump; the system valve, pressure sensor, and mixer module are all built in.

faqs.question: What is the price of the H-Cube® Advance in India?
faqs.answer: The price depends on the gas configuration and fleet modules your application needs. Contact Inkarp for a quotation once your requirements are confirmed.

faqs.question: Who is the authorized distributor of the H-Cube® Advance in India?
faqs.answer: Inkarp is the authorized distributor and service provider for the ThalesNano H-Cube® Advance in India, providing demonstration, installation, training, AMC, spare parts, and technical support.

heroParagraphs: Most flow hydrogenation systems do one thing well: hydrogen, in-situ, and that's it. This one doesn't stop there.

A built-in mass flow controller doses in-situ hydrogen at 99.9% purity, or switches to any of 13 external gases, from oxygen and carbon monoxide to argon and ethylene, through the same external gas inlet.
The water reservoir is external and detachable, so refilling and cleaning don't mean opening the system up. A next-generation single-cell electrolysis design extends cell life and cuts maintenance.

It runs from 0°C to 150°C, atmospheric pressure to 100 bar, and connects to a full fleet: a high-temperature Reactor Module, the 450°C/200 bar Phoenix Flow Reactor, and a Brooks Autosampler for fully automated catalyst screening, all coordinated from one screen.
